items.text: Tristan Chord
Laplace Rehabilitation Center

items.speaker: Laplace Researcher
items.text: Ma'am, listen.

items.speaker: Laplace Researcher
items.text: Can you please put that down first?
Eyes empty, she ignores the researcher's tentative advice and continues to grasp the shard in her palm.
It's a shard of mirror.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: *deep breath*
Her mirror shattered during the "Storm." This is one piece of it.
But she can't recall who broke it.
Perhaps it was some frantic passerby or simply herself.
Kakania fights against her impulse to grasp the shard even tighter. There is already a cut in her hand. It would be best not to make it deeper.
The Foundation made a mistake. They failed to check her handbag for any dangerous items.

items.speaker: Foundation Staff Member I
items.text: Ma'am, the Foundation will accept you as a refugee in accordance with the "Storm" Act.

items.speaker: Foundation Staff Member I
items.text: And according to Article 43, Section 2, of the Act, "If a person has survived the 'Storm' with no obvious side effects, they will be put under quarantine control."

items.speaker: Foundation Staff Member I
items.text: It also says, "Under special circumstances, ask a member of staff involved in immunity protection production to intervene."

items.speaker: Foundation Staff Member I
items.text: So ...

items.speaker: Foundation Staff Member I
items.text: So we've invited Madam Lucy, the lead of immunity equipment production, to come speak with you. Please put down the sharp object and wait—
She's interrupted by the clanging of steel footsteps and a voice from outside the room.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: I have been informed that I am needed here.

items.speaker: Foundation Staff Member I
items.text: Madam Lucy! That was quick.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Hm?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Madam Lucy. Is that you?
The footsteps grow steadily louder until Madam Lucy is standing squarely in the doorframe.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Yes. It is me. And you are ...
Her scanning process finishes within a second.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Ms. Klara Vingler.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: That's right!

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: We've only heard each other over the phone. I'm impressed you recognized me so easily!

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Your name is written on the end of the bed.
She points to the name tag. She had simply scanned the room.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Oh, the name card. Of course. Haha.
The staff member nods and passes the file to Lucy.

items.speaker: Foundation Staff Member I
items.text: I'll leave her to you then, madam. And please be wary of the glass shard in her hand.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Not to worry. A shard of glass cannot harm me.
She reaches out a shiny steel hand to Kakania.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: It is a pleasure to meet you, Ms. Vingler. You are the only one who made the knot and successfully survived the "Storm." I have many questions for you.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Especially about your condition, side effects, and what it felt like in the throes of the "Storm."

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: However, due to my suspension from Laplace, my colleagues will carry out the querying for me. Your answers will be of significant help to my research.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: As a time-traveler, you must have many questions for us as well. I will try my best to answer them for you.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: You're suspended?

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Is that your first question?

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: The answer is yes. I received a suspension order because ...
The robot tilts her head, searching for the reason in her almost-ruined database.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: I violated the confidentiality agreement. I told an arcanist in Vienna about the knot. Her name was ...

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Kakania, I suppose?

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Yes, that seems to be the name.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: How impressive. We have never met before, yet you immediately filled the hole in my data. How did you do that, Ms. Vingler?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Because I'm the one you told—I'm Kakania!

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: What on earth is going on? Have you forgotten about our conversations on the phone?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Good lord, just when I think I've found someone I actually know in this era!
Despite Kakania's increasing panic, Lucy remains remarkably calm.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Do not worry, Dr. Kakania. My memory loss was an inevitable side effect of the "Storm" immunity experiment.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: The data I still have left should be sufficient to answer most of your questions, though some details will be missing.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Are there any other questions you would like to ask me?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Experiment side effects?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I suppose the situation here is no easier than mine.
Realizing the sensitivity of the topic, she doesn't press for more details.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: "Immunity," you said.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Ms. Marcus calls it a catastrophe, and you call it the "Storm." Is it some kind of disease?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Like plague or smallpox?

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: I am unable to answer this question. It is an unknown phenomenon. "Storm," "disease," and "immunity" are just terms we use to try and understand it.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: But an answer I can provide is: This is a disaster of time that covers the world. Only a few areas are unaffected by it. Both its origin and regularity remain unknown.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Using the ritual provided by yourself and Investigator Marcus, we successfully found a method that protects people from the "reverse." Although it has its limits.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: That's it?

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: That is the summary of the situation.
Even the person with the most knowledge on this subject has little understanding.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Our research on "Storm" immunity is still in its initial stages. We are far from fully understanding it.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Details like lineage, the thickness of pneuma where you cast the ritual, and the order you tie the knot may affect the results.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: It is necessary for us to cross-check our data with those who survived the "Storm." Furthermore, you are a crucial witness of the Vienna Incident.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: We hope you will cooperate with the examination and querying, Dr. Kakania.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I understand, madam.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I must thank you. Thank you again for giving me this opportunity. You kept your word and taught me how to tie the knot, but now I have almost nothing to give in return.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I'm simply here as living proof that the possibility of survival is not zero. That's all I have to offer.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I haven't a clue as to how or why it took effect. I'm afraid I'm useless to this place and to you.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Is that so?

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Perhaps there is one thing you can do: undo the hypnosis on Ms. Dittarsdorf.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Isolde?!
She jumps out of bed like a startled bird. Lucy just keeps talking.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Since she is a former member of Manus Vindictae, the Foundation attempted to question Ms. Isolde von Dittarsdorf. However, she did not cooperate, or rather, could not cooperate.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I-Is she alright? I was present for most of what happened, too. Maybe the Foundation can question me instead.
Lucy continues to ignore her.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: In brief, she has been in a state of hypnosis since she arrived at the Foundation. She still believes she is living a regular life in Vienna. Thus, we have made no progress.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Investigator Marcus mentioned in her report that it was you who hypnotized Ms. Dittarsdorf.
Kakania takes a step back in horrified disbelief.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: No, it can't be!

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I hardly ever hypnotize my patients, and when I do, I'm extremely cautious about it. I didn't know it was even possible for hypnosis to last so long!

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: No, I would never make such a rudimentary mistake! W-Would I?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Oh, my! What have I done!

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: We have adopted every known method to undo the hypnosis, but all have failed. We came to the conclusion that you used your arcane skill to hypnotize her. That is why we need your help.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Can you undo her hypnosis by casting your arcane skill?
She stares at Lucy, her breath rasping in her chest, unable to speak through the shock.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Take a deep breath, Dr. Kakania.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: *panting*

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Relax. Try to control the pace of your breathing. Breathe in, breathe out.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: *panting* I, I ...

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I ... *inhale*

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: *exhale* I can't.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: But you have taken a deep breath already.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: No, not that. It's my arcane skill.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I can no longer use it.
Kakania looks down at the shard clenched in her hand. A drop of blood is running down her palm.
She forces herself to look up. With a bitter smile, she presents the shard to Lucy.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: As you said, experiments always have side effects. You lost something. So did I.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: My mirror is broken.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Believe it or not, I cannot use it to cast my arcane skills anymore.
